reader.requirement: Each index-name must be associated with exactly the table whose OCCURS clause names it in INDEXED BY, for every dimension of a multi-dimensional table and for an occurs-depending table, so that SET (formats 1 and 2) and subscripting by it refer to occurrences of that table, and an index-name used to reference a table it is not associated with (§1985:VI.4 line 'can be used to reference only the table to which it is associated') or used as data is refused.

reader.notes: RegisterIndexes binds each INDEXED BY name to an IndexDeclaration owned by its table; DeclaredInHierarchy compares declaration identity, so a same-spelled index of another table is not accepted. Diagnostics cite §2023 clause numbers at --std 85 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-112/src/setswap.cob: 2-D table R3 OCCURS 2 INDEXED BY RX / C3 OCCURS 3 INDEXED BY CX, reference written C3 (CX, RX) with the index-names swapped between dimensions: compiles clean at --std 85 (setswap-002) and --std 2023 (setswap-003) and prints 'd' (CX=2 taken as R3's occurrence, RX=1 as C3's). The reader's requirement claims refusal of 'an index-name used to reference a table it is not associated with' 'for every dimension'. Under §1985:II.4.4.2 ('An index-name can be used to reference only the table to which it is associated via the INDEXED BY phrase'; the index's contents 'correspond to an occurrence number for that specific dimension of the table with which the index is associated') with §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR2 (subscripts in order of successively less inclusive dimensions), CX in the first position references R3's dimension, a table CX is not associated with: an under-rejection. Under the literal §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR3 ('Index-name-1 must correspond to a data description entry in the hierarchy of the table being referenced which contains an INDEXED BY phrase specifying that index-name') CX is in C3's hierarchy and the source is admitted. SubscriptBinder.cs#DeclaredInHierarchy tests hierarchy membership only, by a recorded choice (kb/Work PB459, line 280: 'applied EXACTLY as written ... not on the dimension the subscript position selects'), made from the 2023 text, not the 1985 II.4.4.2 text. The rest holds: setconv.cob SET CX TO RX / SET XD TO CY / SET CX TO XD across dimensions of different size gave occurrence-number results (P1 e, P2 cd, P3 N=3 f); setswap R3 (CX) refused COBOL1961. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.23.4 GR1; OK §1985:II.4.4.2 (both quotations); OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR3; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR2.
